Prints shell code that puts every tool this project declares on PATH for the
current shell session, so they can be run as ordinary commands:

  eval "$(datamitsu source bash)"   # bash / zsh
  datamitsu source fish | source     # fish

Activation downloads nothing: a tool is fetched the first time it is actually
run. Switching branches needs no re-activation — the next tool invocation
notices the config changed and re-resolves itself.

With --config the toolchain comes from a config you name instead of from a
project, so it works outside any repository — a machine-level toolchain for a
shell rc file:

  datamitsu source fish --config ~/.config/datamitsu/datamitsu.config.ts | source

Such a farm never evaluates a project's config: entering a repository's
toolchain stays an explicit datamitsu source in that repository.

stdout carries ONLY shell code. Warnings — tools not downloaded yet, system
binaries this shadows — go to stderr, so the output is always safe to eval.

Usage:
  datamitsu source [flags]
  datamitsu source [command]

Available Commands:
  bash        Print bash activation code
  fish        Print fish activation code
  refresh     Re-bake the project's farm
  status      Show what source mode makes available in this project
  zsh         Print zsh activation code

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for source

Global Flags:
      --before-config strings   Configuration file(s) to load before auto-discovery (for wrappers/libraries)
      --binary-command string   Override the binary command (for npm package wrappers, etc). Can also be set via DATAMITSU_BINARY_COMMAND env var
      --config strings          Additional configuration file(s) to load and merge (can be specified multiple times)
      --log-format string       Status output format: console or jsonl (also via DATAMITSU_LOG_FORMAT)
      --no-auto-config          Disable auto-discovery of datamitsu.config.{js,mjs,ts} at git root
      --no-oci                  Disable OCI bundle store seeding (also via DATAMITSU_NO_OCI)
      --no-parse                Skip output parsers; show tools' raw output instead (also via DATAMITSU_NO_PARSE)
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug-level logging (default level is warn)

Use "datamitsu source [command] --help" for more information about a command.
